key_insight: Hybrid QM/ML calculations reveal how partial dislocations and fault ribbons stabilise prismatic <a> loops in α-Zr, with Fe and H favouring faulted segments and Sn and Nb favouring perfect segments.
engineering_relevance: The findings can inform models of solute trapping and irradiation-induced microstructure evolution in zirconium nuclear fuel cladding.
method: Hybrid quantum mechanics/machine learning modelling of dislocation cores.
Characterisation of nine line segments across three prismatic <a> loop variants.
QM/ML-NEB calculations of glide barriers and faulted-to-perfect transition pathways.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports core geometries, solute-binding preferences and transition mechanisms across nine dislocation line segments, but provides no numerical barriers or validation metrics.
watch_item: Transferability from local segment calculations to evolving loops under reactor irradiation remains to be established.
paper_title: Comprehensive QM/ML Study of Dislocation Loop Line Segments in α-Zr Part I: <a> Loop Core Geometries, Solute Binding, and Transition Barriers
